svg.title: Asset Deal Buyer Protection Architecture
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-asset-deal-protection-architecture; chapter number: 11; title: Asset Deal Buyer Protection Architecture; subtitle: Indemnity, set-off, escrow and allocation around the buyer entity; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Buyer Entity (Asset Purchaser); headcount: 1 acquiring entity, formed to sign the NDAs and LOI, assigned to NewCo at close; focus: Buy assets for liability protection and a stepped-up basis; almost all Main Street and lower middle market deals close as asset sales.; spokes: role: Selling Shareholders; type: Personal indemnitors; kpi: Every selling shareholder signs; indemnity cap 10-15%, deductible 0.5-1%, survival 12-18 months the norm.; role: Seller Note; type: Set-off source; kpi: Sized at 10-15% to match the indemnity cap; never used to set off a working-capital adjustment.; role: Escrow or Holdback; type: Held-back purchase price; kpi: 89% of lower middle market deals carry an escrow, median 10%; SMB escrows likely under 5%.; role: Form 8594 Allocation; type: Matching tax filing; kpi: A $1M intangible amortizes over 15 years; buyer and seller returns must match.; caption: Sellers want stock for capital-gains treatment, buyers want assets, and SMB buyer protection runs on personal indemnity, set-off, escrow and a matched allocation.; assumptions note: Market terms are SMB Law Group's report across roughly 130+ deals and the Aquiem study; practitioners disagree on whether reps carry value without a note to offset.; note: Attributed to SMB Law Group LLP (iNOj__jXGpE at 00:11:52, 00:26:54 and 00:43:34), Walker Deibel (NM-ZwBNBHQE at 00:02:06), Tax Hack Accounting Group (Wd1__Z4Nz6k at 00:02:32) and Teach Me! Personal Finance (G0f0r8tYMnk at 00:05:35).
